task_instance: Build a threat-mitigation mapping for a small web app (an 'Orders API'): map five STRIDE threats to a library of security controls, compute per-threat coverage, run defense-in-depth and control-diversity checks, detect gaps, and generate a mitigation report.
evidence: Read SKILL.md and references/details.md (both present next to each other). The skill is a methodology skill whose reference file gives Python templates for the model (ControlType/ControlLayer/Effectiveness/ImplementationStatus enums, SecurityControl.coverage_score, MitigationMapping coverage + defense-in-depth + control-diversity checks, MitigationPlan gap detection, risk-reduction weighting, and report generation). A few identifier references in the templates were masked by sandbox placeholders, but the full methodology and code structure are readable. Implemented the methodology in mitigation_mapping.py with realistic sample INPUT data (5 STRIDE threats + 6 controls with implementation statuses) and ran it: cd into work dir; python3 -I mitigation_mapping.py. Output and written file mitigation_report.md match. Verified the numbers by hand: T1 credential-stuffing maps to AUTH-001 (VERIFIED, HIGH=3 -> 3.0) and AUTH-002 (IMPLEMENTED, MEDIUM=2 -> 1.6) => 4.6/8 = 57.5%; T3 PII leakage maps only to ENC-001 (NOT_IMPLEMENTED) => 0.0%; overall risk-score-weighted reduction = 35.9%; defense-in-depth flags every threat whose controls sit in a single layer; 5 critical gaps surfaced for the two Critical-impact threats. Files produced: mitigation_mapping.py and mitigation_report.md in the work directory. Core deliverable (a working threat-to-control mapping and report) exists and is verified.
